data.title: Microsoft's (MSFT) Free Cash Flow Expected to Remain Positive Despite Heavy AI Spending
data.description:
Microsoft's (MSFT) free cash flow is expected to remain in positive territory despite the company's heavy spending on artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and infrastructure. In a new report, Bank of America (BAC) singles out Microsoft, saying the Seattle-based company stands alone among major technology companies as one of only a few that isn't expected to post negative free cash flow over the next year.

Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), Oracle (ORCL), and Meta Platforms (META) are each expected to fall into negative free cash flow in 2027, with Bank of America forecasting these so called "hyperscalers" next-twelve-month free cash flow estimates will drop significantly between by 2028 as spending on Ai accelerates.

Microsoft's AI Spending

Microsoft is spending heavily on AI. The company behind the Copilot digital assistant is expected to spend $175 billion to $190 billion in total capital expenditures this year, with the vast majority of that money going towards AI infrastructure such as data centers and microchips. The company is expected to spend even more in 2027.

Promotion

Technology investors who refuse to pick growth or income now have TDAQ.

The company has said that its capital expenditures could reach as much as Microsoft $260 billion in 2027, again with the majority of the money being funneled into AI projects and technologies. Yet despite the heavy spending, Microsoft is expected to continue generating positive free cash flow, distinguishing it from its mega-cap technology peers, says Bank of America.

The outlook isn't entirely bleak for the sector, according to BofA Global Research, which expects hyperscalers' free cash flow to shift from negative to positive by the second half of 2027 as AI-related revenue growth accelerates and AI capital expenditures decelerate.

However, the research firm warns of significant risk: AI capex has surprised to the upside by a much wider margin than revenue—50% versus 20% this year—meaning 2027 expectations imply a marked shift in trend.

BofA Global Research's estimated compute demand through 2030 implies approximately $10T of spend, roughly $2T above current forecasts.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Shopify Stock (SHOP) Has 20% Upside, Says RBC Capital Markets
data.description:
RBC Capital Markets (RY) has raised its price target on the stock of Shopify (SHOP), saying it sees 20% upside in the Canadian e-commerce firm. Paul Treiber, a top five-star-rated analyst, raised his price target on SHOP stock to $200 from $180 previously, citing strong growth momentum. The new price target is 20% higher than where Shopify's stock currently trades. Treiber reiterated a Buy rating on Shopify's shares.

In a note to clients, the RBC analyst said that he sees potential for Shopify's e-commerce platform to exceed market expectations for third-quarter results and fourth-quarter guidance when it reports its latest financial results on Nov. 3. The revised price target on SHOP stock reflects confidence in the company's ability to sustain growth above 30%, added Treiber.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Dips After an Investigation by a U.K. Watchdog
data.description:
Microsoft (MSFT) stock was down 2.45% on Friday after the U.K. watchdog suggested the tech giant needed to be watched more closely. The Competition and Markets Authority believes that Microsoft should be classified as having strategic market status, which would allow more regulatory influence and investigations into the company.

The Competition and Markets Authority reached its conclusion on Microsoft after an investigation was launched in May 2026. The focus of this investigation was Microsoft's software division and whether it was an uncompetitive business. This includes programs such as Excel, Teams, Word, and other apps offered by Microsoft.

The Competition and Markets Authority is interested in Microsoft's business due to how it affects British consumers. That includes the roughly 20 million people who make use of the tech company's software. It also argued there were stark issues that users faced in an attempt to switch away from Microsoft's offerings.

Promotion

Technology believers can stay invested and generate cash flow with TDAQ.

Microsoft's AI operations also came under fire. The company's Copilot was called out by The Competition and Markets Authority as one of the offerings that may be hard for other companies to compete against.

What's Microsoft's Position on This Watchdog's Investigation?

Microsoft doesn't share the same view as The Competition and Markets Authority. Instead, the Windows and Copilot creator told Reuters, "All our products — including Copilot — are open and interoperable, giving customers the ​ability to use them alongside competing services."

Is Microsoft Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Microsoft is Strong Buy, based on 35 Buy and two Hold ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average MSFT stock price target of $601.47, representing a potential 13.96% upside for the shares.

Microsoft stock also received updated analyst coverage today. Five-star StoneX analyst Yi Fu Lee raised his price target for MSFT stock to $600 from $525 and maintained a Buy rating. This new price target represents a potential 13.68% upside for the shares. Lee cited a test of Microsoft Azure in its upcoming earnings report. He's also interested to see how the company's AI development has advanced since its June quarter.

Several other analysts have also updated their price targets for MSFT stock ahead of that earnings report. (See MSFT Stock Forecast)

data.title: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Odds Surge from 30% to 55% in Just 2 Days – Here's Why
data.description:
Prediction market traders are increasingly betting that Elon Musk's tech companies, Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX), will merge. The odds of a deal happening before April 2027 jumped to 55% at the time of writing from 30% on Wednesday, according to Kalshi. The 25-percentage-point increase is likely due to Tesla's flying Roadster demonstration last night, which used technology developed by SpaceX. However, neither company has announced a merger agreement.

Still, the demonstration showed how closely the two businesses are already working together. Tesla's new Roadster used SpaceX-developed thrusters to jump over several parked vehicles at a Texas test facility. The car also accelerated from zero to 60 mph in under one second.

Meanwhile, the prediction market is showing a 41% chance of a merger before March, while the probability of a deal before May stood at 62%.

Promotion

Tesla and SpaceX Already Have Billions of Dollars in Financial Ties

Also fueling the speculation is the fact that Tesla and SpaceX have billions of dollars in financial ties. According to Tesla's financial filings, SpaceX purchased $318 million worth of its Megapack energy storage products during the second quarter. Tesla also invested $2 billion in SpaceX shares in March after its previous investment in xAI was converted into SpaceX stock.

The companies are collaborating on Terafab as well, which is a planned semiconductor manufacturing project in Texas that is expected to cost up to $119 billion. Tesla wants chips for its autonomous vehicles and Optimus humanoid robots, while SpaceX needs computing hardware for its AI operations. This includes the Grok chatbot developed by its subsidiary xAI.

One argument being put forward by analysts is that combining the two companies could simplify decisions about shared projects. However, a merger would require an agreement on how much ownership each group of shareholders receives, as well as the necessary corporate and regulatory approvals.

Is SPCX Stock a Good Buy?

Overall, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on SPCX stock based on 28 Buys, five Holds, and two Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average SPCX price target of $217.50 per share implies 49.5% upside potential. (See SPCX Stock Forecast).

data.title: PDD Stock (PDD) Slumps After Paying $3M to Settle Texan Data Exposure Lawsuit
data.description:
Shares in Chinese e-commerce giant PDD Holdings (PDD) fell 1.24% today after it agreed to pay $3million to the state of Texas and strengthen its data security and product safety practices by using American service providers. The settlement, announced by the state's attorney general Ken Paxton will require PDD's Temu shopping platform to store Texans' personal data on US-based servers controlled by American entities and restrict China-based access, with exceptions for essential business functions. The company was warned that certain data security violations could incur an $8 million annual penalty.

Remove Hazardous Substances

Under the settlement Temu must conduct annual independent product safety testing and remove products found to contain hazardous substances, terminate the sellers and affiliated stores, notify affected Texas consumers and issue full refunds. This is reportedly the first time the company has agreed to keep personal data on US servers and restrict when it can be sent to China.

Under the terms of the settlement, Temu agreed to send only data necessary to fulfilling a transaction, such as shipping addresses, to China. In addition, it will also be required to hire a third party cybersecurity auditor to examine the app's code for malware and spyware.

Paxton sued PDD and Temu in February 2026, alleging that the platform exposed Texans' sensitive data to the Chinese Communist Party and that products sold on the platform could contain harmful chemicals.

Series of U.S. Lawsuits

It is not just in Texas where PDD and Temu are potentially in trouble. Temu faces several lawsuits from U.S. states concerned that the company unlawfully harvests U.S. user data that could be accessed by the Chinese government. Texas is the first to resolve those claims.

Paxton said the settlement also requires Temu "to implement rigorous new product audits and safety standards to protect consumers from dangerous materials in products, including clothing and children's items."

Temu is a significant player in U.S e-commerce. According to Paxton it had more than 82.4 million active users in the United States as of September 2023.

data.title: SpaceX vs. Tesla: Wall Street Sees Over 3X More Upside in One Elon Musk Stock After the Roadster Demo
data.description:
Elon Musk has never been particularly interested in doing things the conventional way. Just when investors think they've seen everything, the billionaire entrepreneur finds another seemingly impossible project to pursue. At SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), that has meant developing reusable rockets, launching the world's largest satellite internet network, and building Starship, a spacecraft designed to eventually carry humans to Mars. And with each technological achievement, Musk seems determined to prove that yesterday's science fiction can become tomorrow's reality.

His latest demonstration, however, didn't involve sending another rocket into orbit. On Thursday, Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) finally unveiled its long-awaited second-generation Roadster at a SpaceX facility in Texas, and this electric sports car did something few expected to see outside a Hollywood movie. Using technology developed alongside SpaceX engineers, the vehicle drove upside down, launched itself into the air, performed an airborne maneuver, and landed safely.

The Roadster, which Tesla now expects to begin producing in 2028, can accelerate from zero to 60 mph in under one second. However, its most spectacular flying configuration won't be available for ordinary road use.

Promotion

High conviction on SPCX? Try Tradr's SPCM or SPCG

For Tesla investors, the demonstration offers another reminder of the company's engineering capabilities and its ability to generate excitement around future products. Yet, the Roadster is unlikely to become a significant revenue contributor anytime soon, particularly as Tesla directs much of its investment toward autonomous driving, Cybercab robotaxis, and humanoid robots.

Meanwhile, the implications for SpaceX are more indirect. The Roadster showcases the potential applications of its propulsion expertise beyond aerospace, while the collaboration could encourage further speculation about a possible merger between Musk's two publicly traded companies.

So, which of Musk's two companies offers the better investment opportunity? Wall Street sees upside potential in both stocks, although analysts expect one to deliver more than three times the gains of the other over the next 12 months.

Tesla's Next Test Goes Beyond the Roadster

Tesla's immediate priorities extend well beyond its newest sports car. The automaker delivered 486,532 vehicles during the third quarter, exceeding market expectations, while energy storage deployments reached 13.7 GWh. Investors will get a clearer picture of profitability when Tesla reports earnings on October 21, with automotive margins, spending, and progress in autonomous driving likely to matter more than the Roadster's flying capabilities.

Wall Street, meanwhile, remains cautiously optimistic about TSLA's prospects. Based on 27 analyst ratings, the stock holds a Moderate Buy consensus, comprising 14 Buys, 11 Holds, and 2 Sells. The average 12-month price target stands at $404.87, suggesting upside of ~14% from current levels. (See TSLA stock forecast)

data.title: Video Game Stocks Traders Need to Watch After This Week's Biggest News
data.description:
Video game stocks were on the move Friday, and investors interested in the space will want to keep up with all the latest news. That includes updates from Microsoft (MSFT), Sony (SONY), Nintendo (NTDOY), Take-Two (TTWO) and others.

1. Xbox and PlayStation Experience a Console Sale Drop

A new report from Circana analyst Mat Piscatella highlighted falling console sales for Microsoft and Sony. The companies' Xbox and PlayStation divisions saw console unit sales fall by 33% and 25% year-over-year, respectively. The analyst warned the U.S. console market hasn't been in such a bad state since the video game crash of the early 1980s. These falling console sales came after price increases for Xbox and PlayStation consoles.

2. Xbox Targets Portable Gaming With a New Controller

Xbox introduced its Nano Controller this week, which is designed for on-the-go gaming. The controller can connect to various devices and is much smaller than a normal Xbox controller. It will launch on November 4, 2026 in major markets and costs $49.99. Preorders for the Nano Controller are currently live.

Promotion

Want cash flow from the tech industry without leaving it? Meet TDAQ.

3. Grand Theft Auto VI PC Port Rumors Excite Gamers

New rumors claim that Take-Two intends to release a PC port of GTA VI sometime in the first quarter of 2027. If true, this would mark one of the quickest releases of a Rockstar game after its console launch. The PlayStation and Xbox versions of GTA VI will be released on November 19, 2026.

4. Leaker Group Threatens to Release the Full GTA VI Story

A group of leakers called CyberLeek has threatened Take-Two with the release of a late GTA VI build before the game comes out next month. This group claims to have a version of GTA VI that includes the full story mode and credits of the game. They want Take-Two to release a physical version of GTA VI and apologize for not doing so. They plan to release the GTA VI build if a crypto token tied to the group has its market value boosted to $30 million.

5. Nintendo Shows Off More of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

Nintendo has given gamers more glimpses of the Ocarina of Time Remake ahead of the game's launch on November 5, 2026. That includes in-depth looks at the world of Hyrule, combat between Link and Dark Link, new fairy hints hidden in the game, and changes compared to the original Ocarina of Time that was released on the Nintendo 64 in 1998. The Ocarina of Time Remake will receive a physical release, as Nintendo has promised to continue to support physical media.

data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Stalls on Tech Weakness as Rate Hike Bets Slip
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 0.24% on Friday as tech stocks continue to sell off while interest rate hike expectations decline. While the Dow is only down slightly, the weakness is much more pronounced in the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 (NDX). Notable losers in both indexes include Salesforce (CRM), Microsoft (MSFT), and Alphabet (GOOGL).

Rate hike odds drifted lower after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh spoke at an International Monetary Fund (IMF) event in Bangkok, Thailand. While Warsh declined to provide hints regarding the central bank's decision at the October 28 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), investors viewed his silence as a dovish stance. "I don't prejudge meetings," he said. "I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year."

The odds of a 25-basis-point hike later this month are now at 17.2%, down from 27.7% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool. At the same time, the odds of at least one hike by the end of the year barely budged, edging lower to 89% from 89.3%.

data.title: Walmart (WMT) Buying American To Boost Red, White, and Blue Manufacturing Power
data.description: Retail giant Walmart (WMT) has revealed it is doing its bit to support American manufacturing by declaring that two-thirds of its annual product spend this year is going on goods made, grown or assembled in the U.S. Walmart revealed the figure while hosting its 13th annual Open Call event where nearly 150 entrepreneurs from 35 states and Puerto Rico pitched their products directly to its and Sam's Club merchants. The Walmart share price, hit by consumer uncertainty, is up just 7% in the year-to-date.
